articles.title: Texas Roadhouse says claims of white employees discussing spitting in Black customers' food in a Facebook group are 'completely unfounded'
articles.summary: US News: Texas Roadhouse clapped back at the viral social media claim that its white servers were discussing spitting in Black customers' food in a private Fac.
articles.body: Texas Roadhouse clapped back at the viral social media claim that its white servers were discussing spitting in Black customers' food in a private Facebook group as a hoax and confirmed that the claims based on which diners raised boycott calls were completely unfounded. The controversy started when an unverified claim originated on Facebook, allegedly from a user warning Black diners to avoid eating at Texas Roadhouse and Logan's Roadhouse. The post alleged that a secret Facebook group boasting over 400,000 white server members existed for the explicit purpose of organizing food contamination targeted at Black customers. Specific accusations claimed that servers were licking their fingers, spitting in saliva, and touching items like the chain's famous fresh rolls before serving them.The controversy escalated as the post went viral and customers called for a nationwide boycott."We are committed to creating an environment where every guest is treated with respect and unreasonable hospitality," Texas Roadhouse officials wrote responding to the outrage. "We do not tolerate discrimination, harassment or mistreatment of any kind, and we expect our Roadies to treat every guest with dignity and care."Texas Roadhouse brought in an independent third-party cybersecurity firm to trace the origins of the post. They confirmed there was no evidence of such a 400,000-member group existing, nor any record of food-tampering incidents linked to the claim.Travis Doster, chief communications officer of Texas Roadhouse, told USA TODAY that some social media users who defamed the chain retracted their statements after it was proved to be a hoax."Thereâs no video of any of our servers," he said. "Thereâs no video of anybody saying they have evidence. Itâs very frustrating because itâs not true." He also suggested the culprit behind the post could be bots, or automated programs that make posts mimicking human engagement online. "There is zero credible evidence this is true,â he said. âThis did not happen in any of our restaurants."Viral post deleted after creating outrageThe original Facebook post was deleted. It was allegedly shared in a Facebook group called "White and proud," where a user named Nancy Smith said they worked at an unidentified Texas Roadhouse location and was in a pact with other White servers at the restaurant to contaminate the food of Black guests.The user said this had been going on for a while, or at least since the April 2025 killing of 17-year-old Austin Metcalf by Black teenager Karmelo Anthony. Anthony has been sentenced to 35 years in prison for the stabbing.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New US sanctions signal Trump desperation on Iran, experts say
articles.summary: Economic escalation is unlikely to force the Iranian government to capitulate to US demands, according to experts.
articles.body:
The United States announced new sanctions on Iran and a slew of global entities doing business with the country on Monday, in what officials have called an “economic D-Day” and officially dubbed “Operation Economic Outcast”, in an effort to force Tehran to negotiate an end to the war.

The announcement followed repeated demands by US President Donald Trump that Iranian leaders take actions like dropping their claims over the Strait of Hormuz and return to talks to end its nuclear programme.

list 1 of 3 Trump’s latest wave of Iran sanctions: Which 60 entities are targeted?

list 2 of 3 US launches Economic war on Iran

list 3 of 3 Sanctions or missiles? How Gulf will view Trump’s new Iran approach

Nearly six months into its war on Iran, the US is seeing little impact from its military operations against the country. Crucial military munitions stocks have been depleted, and important tools used to project power globally have been redirected towards Iran.

The long-term implications of the war, analysts say, have pushed the Trump administration to try economic sanctions, but these are unlikely to compel Iran into meeting the demands.

“The United States is returning to economic pressure because military force has failed to deliver the quick victory it expected,” Negar Mortazavi, senior fellow at the US-based Center for International Policy, told Al Jazeera. “The ‘economic D-Day’ declaration underscores the war’s failure so far to force Iran’s surrender or achieve Washington’s political objectives.”

“On paper, the US and Iran are a huge military mismatch,” Ryan Costello, policy director at the National Iranian American Council (NIAC), told Al Jazeera. “The US caused a lot of destruction with its munitions, but so too did Iran with its missiles and drones. So it is hard to describe the war to date as anything but a catastrophic mistake.”

While the US has killed key Iranian political and military leaders, Tehran has leveraged its geography and vast arsenal of drones and missiles, striking out at key oil and gas infrastructure in a region that has depended on drawing investors by offering stability. And Tehran’s choking of traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has brought pain for consumers as far away as the US, who now pay about 40 percent more at the petrol pump than before the war.

“It was a fundamental miscalculation Trump did in the outset that the threat of war will compel the Iranians to surrender,” Trita Parsi, head of the Washington, DC-based Quincy Institute, told Al Jazeera. “Instead they fought back, and they fought back very hard.”

The US supply of missile interceptors has fallen low, according to experts like those at the Washington, DC-based Center for Strategic and International Studies. In late July, the centre found it would take at least three years for the Pentagon to bring supplies back to pre-war levels. The White House has denied any such shortage exists , but analysts say the problem is very real, even if it is temporary, and the Pentagon has been forced to redirect resources away from adversaries like China.

That has included US aircraft carriers. The Pentagon has pulled a key asset away from China , dispatching the USS George Washington from Japan to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Gulf, whose sailors have been at sea for months longer than planned because of the war.

Key US bases in the region – including the Navy’s Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain – have been damaged or become unsafe for use, adding hundreds of kilometres to supply lines as ships look as far away as the Indian Ocean island of Diego Garcia for sourcing.

“In my judgement, the US Armed Forces have probably permanently lost access to 15 Persian Gulf bases,” retired US Army four-star general Barry R McCaffrey wrote on X.

“I think it became clear the US is running out of runway on this, so the administration pivoted to what it knows best, or has perceived as effective in the past, which is these economic tools,” said Jamal Abdi, head of the NIAC. “Really, it’s a way for the administration to scale back to where it was before this war but present it as this new enhanced pressure policy.”

‘Why would I want to blow up the global financial system?’

Instead of hitting Iran and others doing business with it, Monday’s sanctions announcement turned out to be little more than yet another warning, analysts say. While the US Department of the Treasury did sanction 60 new individuals and entities from around the globe over their business with Iran, it did not include major Chinese banks or others that help Tehran sell its oil.

At least 90 percent of Iran’s crude oil exports end up in China, netting Tehran tens of billions of dollars in revenue. Ending that trade would need the US to confront China far more directly than it is willing to do. In fact, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent admitted exactly that on Monday, when he responded to a question from reporters about why the US did not immediately announce sanctions on Chinese entities long known to facilitate oil trade.

“Why would I want to blow up the global financial system?” Bessent responded.

“To me, it’s more a psychological operation than an actual warfare,” Sina Azodi, assistant professor of Middle East Politics at the George Washington University, told Al Jazeera. “It will have an impact, there’s no question, and I’m sure it’s going to scare off people and affect Iran’s economy by creating more chaos and adding uncertainty … but I don’t think it will ultimately change Iranian calculations in the short term.”

Pain for the Iranian people, gain for Washington?

The new US measures seek to expand the scope of already broad restrictions against the Iranian economy, adding the possibility of secondary sanctions against non-Iranian entities dealing with sectors like digital assets, gold, technology, aviation and shipping.

Tensions with Washington have already forced Iranians to contend with things like shortages of medicine and higher fuel prices . Many of the new sectors being targeted are crucial for common Iranians looking to find ways around previous sanctions, analysts point out. Gold can help preserve wealth as the Iranian rial tumbles. Digital assets like cryptocurrencies let relatives send and receive money across borders. Airlines let Iranians visit relatives abroad, or check on loved ones inside the country.

Quincy Institute’s Parsi said he doubts new sanctions would have an impact on the Iranian government, but they will on the Iranian people.

“I think they will likely be quite impactful and painful for the Iranian people,” he said. “But translating that pain into a shift in their policy is a completely different thing.”

He pointed out that the Trump administration has long known how Tehran reacts to attempts to squeeze it economically. During his first term in 2019, Trump was engaged in an online war with Iran, and economic measures tried to exert more pressure on Tehran, prompting Iran-backed Houthi forces to hit tankers in the Gulf as well as oilfields in Saudi Arabia .

Experts say if Iran’s back is against the wall, it will retaliate.

“If the point of these sanctions is to force them to capitulate, then from what we see in the past, the Iranians would rather escalate than capitulate,” Parsi said.

The attempted use of new sanctions will end up further exposing the limits of US power in the conflict, said the Center for International Policy’s Mortazavi.

“The sanctions will deepen the economic pain facing ordinary Iranians. But years of maximum pressure have shown that economic hardship does not automatically translate into political capitulation,” she said. “If anything, this move exposes the limits of the war: Washington can continue raising the costs for Iran, but it has yet to force Tehran to change course.”

Meanwhile, the continued failure to force Iran to give up has not only made the war itself unpopular in the US, but it has also yielded the lowest approval ratings ever for Trump himself, with just 31 percent of Americans supporting the war, and 33 percent approving of the president’s performance, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll.

With US midterm elections just a few months away, that is something leaders in Tehran are well aware of, said George Washington University’s Azodi.

“They calculate ahead of midterm elections in the US that the Trump administration is not going to have an appetite for more conflict,” he said. “Iran is most likely going to try to weather the storm, absorb the pain, until the Trump administration gives them a good offer.”

articles.title: Quote of the day by Aristotle: âThe man of practical wisdom aims at avoiding pain, not at attaining pleasure"
articles.summary: Rest of World News: The pursuit of pleasure is often treated as one of life's simplest goals, but Aristotle offered a more measured view of what it means to live wisely. .
articles.body: The pursuit of pleasure is often treated as one of life's simplest goals, but Aristotle offered a more measured view of what it means to live wisely. In his Nicomachean Ethics, Aristotle wrote: âThe man of practical wisdom aims at avoiding pain, not at attaining pleasure.â The statement appears in his discussion of pleasure, pain and self-control, where he considers whether pleasure should be treated as the highest good. Aristotle's argument suggests that practical wisdom is not simply about seeking whatever feels good in the moment. Instead, it involves understanding which desires are worth following and recognising when the pursuit of pleasure can ultimately create greater difficulties. His words remain relevant because modern life constantly encourages people to seek comfort, entertainment and immediate satisfaction. The quote offers a reminder that wisdom can sometimes mean choosing what prevents unnecessary pain rather than constantly pursuing what feels pleasurable.Quote of the day by Aristotle: What did Aristotle mean by the quote?Aristotle's statement centres on the difference between practical wisdom and the pursuit of immediate pleasure. In Nicomachean Ethics, he discusses the way people respond to pleasure and pain and examines the behaviour of those who lack self-control. His point is not that all pleasure is bad or that a wise person should live without enjoyment. Instead, Aristotle distinguishes between pleasures that are beneficial and excessive or misguided pleasures that can lead to problems. The practically wise person therefore does not make pleasure the sole objective. Such a person understands that avoiding unnecessary pain can be more important than chasing temporary enjoyment.The idea becomes clearer when considered alongside Aristotle's broader discussion of self-control. He argues that people can become overly driven by pleasurable things and that this pursuit can itself produce pain. Someone who constantly seeks immediate gratification may eventually face consequences that outweigh the original pleasure. Practical wisdom therefore requires judgement. It means considering where a particular choice will lead rather than evaluating it only by how enjoyable it feels in the present. Aristotle's message is ultimately about moderation, foresight and the ability to place short-term desires within the context of a larger and more balanced life.Why avoiding unnecessary pain can be a form of wisdomPeople often associate wisdom with achieving more, gaining more or experiencing more pleasure. Aristotle's observation presents another way of looking at it. Sometimes the wiser decision is the one that prevents avoidable problems from developing in the first place. A person may choose discipline over excess, restraint over impulse or preparation over convenience because these choices can reduce difficulties later. This does not mean avoiding every challenge. Some difficulties are necessary for growth, and Aristotle's wider philosophy places considerable importance on developing good character through practice and habit. The point is to distinguish between worthwhile difficulty and unnecessary suffering. Practical wisdom helps a person recognise that difference and make choices accordingly.This idea remains relevant in everyday decisions. Eating or spending excessively may provide immediate pleasure but create problems later. Avoiding difficult responsibilities may feel comfortable in the moment but increase stress over time. Similarly, constantly choosing entertainment over meaningful work can offer short-term satisfaction while making long-term goals harder to achieve. Aristotle's argument encourages people to look beyond the immediate emotional reward and consider the consequences of their choices.Why chasing pleasure does not always lead to happinessAristotle's discussion is particularly interesting because he does not simply argue that pleasure is worthless. In Nicomachean Ethics, he examines different arguments about pleasure and ultimately treats pleasure as having an important place in human life. His concern is with the assumption that every pleasurable experience should automatically be pursued. Some pleasures can be excessive, harmful or connected to desires that undermine self-control.This distinction is important in a world where instant gratification is increasingly accessible. Entertainment, shopping, food, social media and other forms of stimulation can provide immediate rewards with very little effort. Yet the fact that something is enjoyable does not necessarily mean that pursuing more of it will improve a person's life. Aristotle's idea encourages a more deliberate approach. Instead of asking only whether something feels good, a person can also ask whether it is good for them, whether it supports their goals and whether the consequences are worth the temporary pleasure.Aristotle and the importance of practical wisdomPractical wisdom, or phronesis, occupies an important place in Aristotle's ethical philosophy. It concerns the ability to deliberate well about how to act in particular circumstances. Rather than relying on simple rules, practical wisdom involves judging what is appropriate in a given situation and choosing actions that contribute to a good life. Aristotle's discussion of pleasure and pain forms part of this wider examination of human behaviour, virtue and self-control.The quote therefore should not be interpreted as a simple instruction to avoid discomfort at all costs. A wise person may willingly accept temporary pain or difficulty when it serves a worthwhile purpose. Studying can be difficult, exercise can be uncomfortable and achieving an important goal can require sacrifice. The wisdom lies in understanding which difficulties are meaningful and which forms of pain are simply the consequences of poor choices. Aristotle's approach asks people to think beyond immediate feelings and consider the broader consequences of their actions.The timeless lessonAristotle's words ultimately encourage a more thoughtful relationship with pleasure and pain. A good life is not necessarily one in which every moment is comfortable or every desire is satisfied. Wisdom involves knowing when to pursue something, when to exercise restraint and when avoiding a particular choice can save us from greater difficulties later. The quote reminds us that self-control is not about rejecting pleasure but about refusing to let pleasure control our decisions. In a culture increasingly focused on instant gratification, Aristotle's ancient observation offers a simple but powerful lesson: sometimes the wisest choice is not the one that promises the greatest pleasure, but the one that prevents unnecessary pain and helps us live with greater balance and judgement.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Best hiking trails near Scott Stadium in Charlottesville: a guide for Virginia football fans
articles.summary: Before the Cavaliers kick off at Scott Stadium, explore Humpback Rocks, the Blue Hole swimming spot, and Shenandoah National Park all within 35 minutes.
articles.body: Week 0 | NC State at Virginia | Saturday, Aug. 29 | Scott Stadium, Charlottesville, VA | 3:30 p.m. ET Funny how things work out. This game was supposed to be college football's first trip to South America, with NC State and Virginia set to kick off Week 0 at Nilton Santos Stadium in Rio de Janeiro. Then the whole thing fell apart this summer when Athlete Advantage (the event organizer) told the ACC it simply couldn't pull it off. So the Wolfpack and Cavaliers got rerouted back to the far less exotic — but far more practical — Blue Ridge foothills of Charlottesville instead. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS Virginia's loss of a trip to Rio is your gain. Instead of fighting for a spot on a flight to Brazil, you can be standing on a mountaintop overlooking the Shenandoah Valley by 9 a.m. and in your tailgate spot by 1. Charlottesville sits right up against the Blue Ridge Parkway and the edge of Shenandoah National Park, which means some of the best hiking in Virginia is closer to Scott Stadium than most fans realize. Here's where to go — all within an hour of kickoff and none requiring a passport or conversational Portuguese. Saunders-Monticello Trail 10 minutes from Scott Stadium | Easy The one to bring the whole crew, including grandparents and strollers. A 4.4-mile out-and-back on packed gravel and raised boardwalk, climbing gently through forest canopy up to the visitor center at Thomas Jefferson's Monticello. Dog-friendly, wheelchair-accessible and shaded most of the way. If anyone in your group wants to actually tour the house, that's a separate ticket — $23 to $30 for adults, $10 for kids 5 to 11 — but the trail itself is free. Blue Ridge Tunnel 30 minutes from Scott Stadium | Easy A change of pace from the usual mountain-view hike: a 4.6-mile out-and-back through an actual 1850s railroad tunnel carved straight through the mountain under Rockfish Gap. Bring a flashlight or headlamp — it gets really dark in there, and the temperature drops the deeper you go, which is an added bonus. BEAT THE HEAT: HERE ARE SOME OF THE BEST TIPS TO AVOID HEATSTROKE DURING A HIKE THIS SUMMER Shenandoah National Park (Rockfish Gap entrance) 25 minutes from Scott Stadium | $30 per vehicle | Moderate If you're only going to spend money on one thing this weekend besides the game, this is the one worth it. The Rockfish Gap entrance drops you right onto Skyline Drive, with two standout hikes an easy detour apart: Calvary and Chimney Rocks at milepost 90, a short trek out to a flat-topped rock overlook, and Turk Mountain at milepost 93.5, which delivers rock scrambles and real mountain views for the effort. Being a national park, it will cost you an entry fee of $30 per vehicle, which is good for seven days. Sugar Hollow Reservoir & the Blue Hole 35 minutes from Scott Stadium | Moderate The pick if you’re looking to do a little soaking. A 3-mile out-and-back from the Sugar Hollow parking area leads to the Blue Hole, a genuinely beautiful swimming hole on the Moormans River. This spot keeps showing up on the "best swimming holes in Virginia" lists for a reason. Bring water shoes; the rocks get slick. If your crew wants more of a workout instead, a separate 4.6-mile route from the same lot heads out to Big Branch Falls through a shaded forest. Humpback Rocks 30 minutes from Scott Stadium | Moderate-strenuous The payoff hike, and the one most worth setting an alarm for. It's a brutal, steep mile straight up, but the reward is a 360-degree view across the Shenandoah Valley and Blue Ridge that's tough to beat anywhere in the state. This is the one hike on the list with zero shade at the top, so this is the one to knock out at sunrise, not after brunch. Sunrise at Humpback is a bucket-list item for many UVA students. Crabtree Falls 60–75 minutes from Scott Stadium | $3 day-use fee | Moderate-strenuous Crabtree Falls is a series of five major cascades tumbling a total of 1,200 feet down the mountainside. For context, that's taller than the Eiffel Tower. And the longest single cascade in that series drops 400 feet, enough to make Crabtree Falls the tallest single vertical-drop waterfall east of the Mississippi. The hike up alongside it is a 3-mile round trip with switchbacks and handrails at the steeper spots. It's genuinely one of the most photographed trails in Virginia. The catch: this one runs 60 to 75 minutes from Scott Stadium depending on route and traffic. If you're rolling into Charlottesville just for the game, Crabtree probably isn't the move. But if you're making a weekend of it and have an extra day before or after, it's worth the drive. We should probably also mention there's another Crabtree Falls off the Blue Ridge Parkway in North Carolina. Make sure you're plugging the right one into your GPS. Truthfully, you can't go wrong no matter which trail you choose. Between the Blue Ridge Parkway, Shenandoah National Park and a reservoir system that seems to have a trail wrapped around every corner of it, Charlottesville is about as good as it gets for outdoor adventurers who also happen to love college football. This was opposed by advocate Varun Thakur, who said the law was settled by SC.The SG said Centre was not seeking review or modification of the judgement but wanted to apprise the court of field-level difficulties in retrospective implementation. The SG said this would require changing the status of older batches of creamy layer OBC candidates to non-creamy and warrant change in cadre, post and service in civil services. It would also necessitate corresponding changes for an equal number of candidates who had long been serving in a cadre and service like IFS, IAS and IPS, and result in chaos.Mehta said he was only requesting early listing before a bench of Justices P S Narasimha and R Mahadevan. CJI agreed to list the applications on Sept 1.In its application, Centre said, âOn account of the serious challenges and implications with the implementation of the directions of SC, govt is committed to bring out a policy which will effectively address the observations made by SC, while also ensuring that the direct and indirect impact of the policy is fair and just.âIf the March 11 judgement is implemented without suitable policy intervention it will have a far-reaching impact on govt recruitments and admissions in higher education institutions undertaken by central as well as 18 state/UT govts, it said.Govt said major bodies/employers â like Railways, banks, the department of posts and paramilitary â would also be flooded with hundreds of thousands of representations/litigations seeking retrospective reclassification of the creamy layer.Following the Indra Sawhney judgement in 1992, govt had issued an office memorandum on Sept 8, 1993, prescribing the criteria for identifying the OBC creamy layer who would be excluded from reservation benefits.In its March 11 judgement, SC had also observed that the determination of the creamy layer status must be based on the occupational categories specified in the 1993 office memorandum and the income of parents employed in private sector organisations could not automatically lead to the conclusion that the candidate belonged to the creamy layer.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: FICO credit scores are holding up, but consumers are under pressure
articles.summary: Experts say that despite minimal changes to the average FICO score, affordability remains a key issue for many Americans.
articles.body:

Americans' average FICO credit score is holding steady, but experts say this number masks some affordability pressures and reveals how rising costs are shaping their financial decisions.

Today, the average U.S. FICO score sits at 714, down one point from a year ago but unchanged from October 2025, according to a new FICO® Score Credit Insights report.

A FICO credit score is a three-digit number that reflects the information in your credit reports and considers your payment history, amounts owed, credit history length, new credit, and credit mix. This score is used by lenders to make decisions about whether you qualify for mortgages, credit cards, loans, and more.

The report serves as a snapshot of consumers' credit health as rising costs tied to auto loans, housing, and credit cards put pressure on household budgets.

Affordability remains a struggle for many Americans, particularly among lower-scoring and thin-file borrowers.

The report showed that the average monthly payment for a first-time home buyer increased 57% since 2019, and mortgage balances for borrowers with scores below 620 have grown 43% since April 2019.

Auto loan balances for the lowest-scoring borrowers were also up 36%, and subsequent 90-plus-day delinquency rates for both mortgages and autos rose exclusively in the lowest-score bands, remaining flat across all higher score ranges.

"The stability we're seeing in the national average FICO score isn't necessarily because things have gotten easier for consumers — costs have risen across nearly every credit product people use, from mortgages to auto loans to credit cards," said Tommy Lee, senior director at FICO. "What's kept the average steady is that delinquency has actually improved or held steady across every major loan type. That's a story about financial discipline under pressure, not economic ease."

Delinquency remained stable or improved across most products, according to the FICO report. The share of mortgage borrowers in early-stage delinquency eased from 1.42% to 1.35% year over year, while 30-day auto delinquency improved by 5 basis points to 2.6%.

This comes on the heels of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's quarterly report on household debt and credit , which showed that credit card balances rose by $21 billion to stand at $1.26 trillion — a 1.7% increase from the previous quarter and nearing last year's high of $1.28 trillion.

Some of the strategies Americans are using to cover costs include using buy now, pay later services to keep large expenses from straining their budgets and relying on others for ongoing financial support.

Even so, it seems many Americans are still prioritizing their financial health, with nearly three-quarters of Americans checking their FICO scores multiple times a year.

"Younger consumers in particular are treating credit as a tool they're actively managing, not something that happens to them," Lee said. "That said, things have not been easy for younger generations."

He said that about 74% of Gen Z consumers rely on some form of financial support, most often from parents, and, more broadly, 37% of all Americans say the same, with 19% citing parents specifically.

"And 68% of Gen Z homeowners told us housing costs have made it harder to keep up with other expenses," Lee said. "The credit gains are real, but they're happening alongside — not in spite of — meaningful financial strain."

Tips to build and maintain a healthy FICO score

According to FICO, most creditors will consider your scores "good" if they fall between 670 and 739 (on a scale of 300 to 850), with higher scores signaling a lower-risk applicant and lower scores signaling a higher-risk applicant.

Some of the best ways to maintain a healthy score include:

Making payments on time: Payment history is the most heavily weighted factor in your score calculation, so it's important to make payments on time and avoid late or missed payments, defaults, charge-offs, collections, bankruptcies, and foreclosures.

Making more than the minimum payment to reduce your credit utilization : The second most important factor in your FICO score is the amounts owed or how much credit you're using. Working to reduce your balances by making extra payments or paying more than the minimum amount can boost your score.

Limiting new credit applications : Each time you apply for a new credit card or loan, it will result in a hard inquiry. Too many hard inquiries in a short amount of time can negatively impact your score, so it's best to avoid new applications unless absolutely necessary.

articles.title: How Nathan Straus transformed philanthropy and helped make pasteurised milk the safer choice for children
articles.summary: US News: Long before pasteurised milk became a routine part of American life, families in New York faced a serious and often overlooked public-health danger, c.
articles.body: Long before pasteurised milk became a routine part of American life, families in New York faced a serious and often overlooked public-health danger, contaminated milk. In the late 19th and early 20th centuries, raw milk could carry harmful pathogens and was especially dangerous for infants and young children. One wealthy businessman, Nathan Straus, used his fortune and business experience to tackle the problem in an unconventional way. Rather than simply donating money to charities, Straus created a system that combined philanthropy with practical retail distribution. He established milk laboratories and depots where pasteurised and refrigerated milk could be sold cheaply or provided free to families who could not afford it. His campaign eventually helped push pasteurisation into mainstream public-health policy and left a lasting mark on how Americans understood safe milk.Nathan Straus turned his business experience towards philanthropyNathan Straus was born in 1848 and became wealthy through his involvement with major New York department stores, including Abraham and Straus and R.H. Macy and Co. After building his fortune, he and his wife, Lina Gutherz Straus, increasingly devoted their attention to philanthropic causes. The New York Public Libraryâs papers document his work in public health, milk pasteurisation, tuberculosis prevention and assistance to people affected by poverty and disasters. Strausâs approach to charity differed from the traditional model of simply handing out money. During the economic depression of the 1890s, he used his experience in merchandising to establish depots near New Yorkâs poorer neighbourhoods, where essential goods could be provided at reduced prices. This practical approach later shaped his campaign for safer milk. His interest in milk became particularly personal and urgent. At the time, milk could spoil during transportation and storage, while contaminated supplies could expose children to dangerous diseases. Straus believed that improving the way milk was processed and distributed could save lives.The milk crisis that put children at riskIn New York City during the 1890s, infant mortality was extraordinarily high. Raw milk was considered one of the major risks because it could contain disease-causing organisms, including bacteria associated with tuberculosis. Although scientists already understood that heating milk could destroy harmful microorganisms, pasteurisation was not yet universally accepted. Straus became one of its most determined advocates. In 1892, he established the Nathan Straus Pasteurized Milk Laboratory in New York at his own expense. The facility produced safer milk and helped establish a distribution network designed specifically to reach families in poorer parts of the city. His milk depots did more than sell a product. They made pasteurised and refrigerated milk accessible to people who might otherwise have had little choice but to purchase cheaper, potentially unsafe supplies. Some milk was sold below wholesale prices, while families unable to pay could receive it without charge. The NYPL collection includes records of the laboratory and its milk depots, including reports, brochures, instructions for mothers, infant-formula recipes and even coupons that could be redeemed at the depots.âRetail givingâ made philanthropy practicalStrausâs method has since been described as a form of âretail givingâ because it applied the efficiency of business to a social problem. Instead of creating a conventional charity dependent entirely on handouts, he developed a system capable of producing, pricing and distributing a health-protective product on a large scale. The approach also included education. Information was provided to mothers about infant care and the safe handling of milk, while doctors and nurses were involved in advising families. Straus supported efforts to demonstrate that pasteurisation could protect children without sacrificing the nutritional value of milk. His work expanded well beyond New York. According to historical accounts of his philanthropy, Straus and his wife ultimately helped establish hundreds of milk stations across numerous American cities. The NYPL collection records his efforts to promote pasteurisation through speeches, articles, medical and public-health meetings, and advocacy for legislation. The strategy was significant because it connected individual access to safer milk with a broader public-health campaign. Families could obtain pasteurised milk immediately, while policymakers and health professionals were exposed to evidence supporting wider adoption.From a private campaign to a public-health standardStrausâs campaign unfolded at a time when public-health officials were increasingly concerned about infant mortality and infectious disease. His work helped demonstrate the practical benefits of making pasteurised milk available to communities that needed it most. The wider movement eventually contributed to changes in public policy. By the early 20th century, pasteurisation was gaining much greater acceptance among American health authorities, and governments increasingly moved towards requiring safer milk supplies. Straus did not single-handedly make American milk safe, but his efforts formed an important part of a much larger public-health transformation. His particular contribution was showing that philanthropy could operate at the point where a public-health problem actually affected people's daily lives: the purchase and consumption of food.A forgotten legacy in American public healthNathan Straus died in 1931, but the records preserved his legacy is striking because the solution he promoted now seems ordinary. Today, consumers generally expect commercially sold milk to have undergone safety controls that were far from universal when Straus began his campaign. What made his philanthropy distinctive was its practical focus. He did not simply ask how much money could be donated to a cause. He asked how a wealthy businessman could use the systems of production, distribution and retail to make a basic necessity safer and more affordable. That approach helped transform milk from a potential source of serious disease into a much safer staple for American families. In doing so, Straus showed how targeted philanthropy could influence not only individual lives but also the development of public-health practices that eventually reached far beyond the people his original milk stations served.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Dolly Parton through the years, in photos: From ‘9 to 5’ secretary to ‘Hannah Montana’ godmother
articles.summary: Until she died Tuesday at age 80, Dolly Parton was the beloved Queen of Country music.
articles.body: Dolly Parton craved the camera. And until she died Tuesday at age 80, the Queen of Country’s life unspooled in photograph after photograph, turning the poor little girl with the angelic voice from eastern Tennessee into one of America’s most beloved — and recognizable — figures. It was country singer Porter Wagoner who first introduced Parton to a wider audience when he invited her in 1967 to appear on his hit TV show. By 1974, Parton was out on her own, and her signature public image — the blond wigs, the cleavage-baring outfits that showed off her hourglass figure — was cast in stone. Soon Hollywood beckoned, and Parton took it by storm, winning a Grammy for her single “Here You Come Again” and appearing in a string of hit movies that eventually earned her a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1984. Bubbly and witty, Parton was also a must-book guest on the small screen: She made more than 400 television appearances, performing on variety shows hosted by the likes of Cher and Mac Davis, and charming late-night and daytime hosts ranging from Johnny Carson and his successor, Jay Leno, to Oprah Winfrey and Conan O’Brien. Parton also hosted not one, but two TV variety shows, both called “Dolly,” which millions of Americans tuned in to watch. And in 1989, she even took a turn at hosting “Saturday Night Live,” where, during the opening monologue, the running gag was her cracking jokes while the cameraman was unable to focus on anything but her bosom. Her duets with performers ranging from Elton John and Kenny Rogers to Miley Cyrus spanned the generational divide; she became the rarest of performers — one whose fan base expanded as she grew older. With the acclaim came the awards, the invitations to give commencement speeches, the honorary degrees, the chance to perform before thousands of fans at big-time sports events. But there was a part of Parton’s life she mostly kept hidden from America’s prying eyes, the part she is said to have cherished most — her nearly 59-year marriage to her husband, Carl Dean, who died in March 2025. Dean almost never appeared in public with his famous wife and, as a result, there were very few photos of them together available to the public. And they were fine with that. “I’ve kept [my marriage] very personal and sacred and I try to keep my husband out of the business,” she said in an interview. “That’s not what he chose to do, he just happened to love me and I love him enough to not expose him to it.”

articles.title: US lawmakers urge Trump team to free American student held by Israel
articles.summary: Congress members call on Marco Rubio to ‘use every tool’ at his disposal to secure release of 20-year-old Sama Safi.
articles.body:
More than 40 members of the United States Congress have penned a letter to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio calling on him to push for the release of Sama Safi, a 20-year-old US citizen who has been detained by the Israeli military since June.

The legislators warned on Tuesday that the Palestinian American student's health is deteriorating "under appalling conditions" in Israeli custody.

"Every day that Sama remains wrongfully detained in these inhumane conditions, she is at greater risk of irreversible and life-threatening repercussions," the lawmakers, led by Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib , wrote to Rubio.

"Her life is at risk on your watch. We urge you to act swiftly and use every tool at your disposal to secure the immediate release of Sama Safi so that she can receive the medical care she urgently needs and return to her family, her studies, and the life and freedom that every 20-year-old deserves."

Six US senators – including Elizabeth Warren, Bernie Sanders and Chris Van Hollen – signed on to the letter alongside dozens of members of the House of Representatives.

articles.body: A 58-foot fishing boat ran aground at a popular Northern California beach — prompting a closure as crews worked to remove roughly 1,000 gallons of diesel from the vessel. The Lake Bay became stranded early Friday at North Beach in Point Reyes National Seashore, according to an alert from the National Park Service (NPS). The boat was carrying 40,000 pounds of squid at the time, Inverness resident Richard James told the Point Reyes Light, a local newspaper, citing a conversation with the vessel's skipper. No injuries, fuel leaks or impacts to wildlife were reported, the agency said. Fox News Digital reached out to the NPS for further comment and details. The Lake Bay can hold up to 2,800 gallons of fuel. It was reported to have approximately 1,000 gallons of diesel on board, according to a press release from the U.S. Coast Guard. Crews were coordinating with the party responsible for the vessel and a contracted salvage company to remove the fuel, the Coast Guard said. 75-FOOT BOAT SURFS WAVE, RUNS AGROUND IN HAWAII Capt. (He is not connected to or involved with the Lake Bay fishing boat.)  With 40,000 pounds of squid reportedly onboard, Moran said removing the catch could present another challenge. articles.title: Red Sox Explain Adley Rutschman's Elbow Discomfort and Scheduled Day Off
articles.summary: Backup Boston Red Sox catcher Connor Wong will take over behind the plate for Adley Rutschman.
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox decided to go all in at this year's trade deadline, sending a significant prospect package to the Baltimore Orioles for catcher Adley Rutschman .

Now in his fifth big-league season, Rutschman is already one of the most accomplished backstops of his era. He earned his third career All-Star selection this year and when available has excelled in all aspects of the game.

Across 79 games, the 28-year-old switch-hitting catcher has posted a .236 batting average, .320 on-base percentage, .726 OPS, nine home runs and 51 RBIs while continuing to play elite defense at a premium position.

Despite his track record, Rutschman's time in Boston is off to a slow start as he gets acclimated to his new team. He has also been gradually working his way back into a rhythm after spending time on the injured list.

At the time of the trade, Rutschman was sidelined with left wrist inflammation, which marked his third IL stint of the season alone.

Given how Rutschman has struggled to stay healthy, the Red Sox have routinely given him scheduled days off since his arrival. That figured to be the case for Tuesday's game against the Miami Marlins as Connor Wong took over behind the plate.

However, manager Chad Tracy announced the real reason when speaking with reporters during pregame.

Rutschman's removal was due to feeling discomfort in his right elbow, though Tracy did add that there is no concern, per Christopher Smith of MassLive.

articles.title: Two unvaccinated people in Pennsylvania are first measles-related deaths in US this year
articles.summary: Pennsylvania reported two deaths related to measles as an outbreak there approaches 400 cases, the state Department of Health said Tuesday. Both were unvacci...
articles.body:
Pennsylvania reported two deaths related to measles as an outbreak there approaches 400 cases, the state Department of Health said Tuesday. Both were unvaccinated.

These are the first US deaths related to measles reported in 2026 and the first in Pennsylvania in 35 years.

"My deepest sympathies are with the loved ones who are facing this unimaginable loss," Secretary of Health Dr. Debra Bogen said in a statement. "As a physician, I want to make sure that people understand that the MMR vaccine is safe and provides the best protection we have against measles."

The deaths come as US Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has led efforts to make sweeping changes to federal vaccine recommendations, including those involving the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine. During Kennedy's time in office, vaccination rates have continued to fall nationwide, leaving more children vulnerable to preventable illness.

In 2021, Kennedy – who was then leading the anti-vaccine organization Children's Health Defense – visited Lancaster County, where he made light of his own childhood case of measles and stoked fears in vaccines, which he suggested were causing autism and autoimmune diseases.

On Tuesday, Kennedy called Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro to offer federal staff to help with the measles response, but Shapiro said he declined because he thought the state could manage with its own resources. He said he also told Kennedy that the disinformation he spread about vaccines was having repercussions.

"There's real-life consequences to spreading misinformation. There's real-life consequences to scaring people and not relying on actual doctors and actual medical professionals to provide unbiased information to parents so that we can make reasonable decisions for our kids," Shapiro said in a news briefing.

"Sharing conspiracy theories and misinformation does not help the cause of public health, and it leaves people less healthy and less safe, and it leaves parents in a position where it's harder for us to do our jobs to protect our children," he added.

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said on social media that it "is working closely with state and local health departments to strengthen response efforts, rapidly support affected communities across the state, and communicate the steps people can take to slow the spread of measles. The MMR vaccine provides the most effective protection against measles and helps prevent its spread. CDC will continue to follow Pennsylvania's lead and provide resources to support the state's response."

Both of the Pennsylvania deaths were in residents of Lancaster County. Health officials said they will not release any additional details.

Pennsylvania has confirmed 393 measles cases in 28 counties in 2026, Bogen said in a news conference Tuesday. Roughly half of them have been in Lancaster County, she said.

About 20% of cases in Pennsylvania this year have required hospitalization. Among measles cases confirmed by the health department, none have been in people who have received both recommended doses of the MMR vaccine, she added.

The highly contagious virus has continued its historic resurgence in the US this year, with a second record-breaking year in a row. The country has recorded more cases than 2,700 cases this year, more than any other year since 1991 – surpassing a grim milestone that was just topped last year.

The disease was declared eliminated in the US in 2000, but more cases have been recorded in the past year and a half than there have been in the previous 25 years combined. Experts expect that the US will soon lose its elimination status, the recognition by the World Health Organization that measles is no longer transmitting regularly within a country.

Early symptoms of measles include fever, cough, runny nose and red, watery eyes, Pennsylvania health officials said, and a rash follows a few days later, starting on the head and spreading downward. Symptoms can start seven to 21 days after exposure.

Measles can spread when an infected person breathes, coughs or sneezes, and the virus remains infectious in the air and on surfaces for up to two hours after the person with infection leaves the area.

Measles can cause serious short- and long-term health problems, including pneumonia and brain swelling. Death related to measles are rare but happen in 1 to 3 patients per 1,000 cases.

"People have forgotten how serious it can be, especially for the very young, the pregnant and the very old," Bogen said.

Two doses of the MMR vaccine are 97% effective against measles. Pennsylvania health officials are recommending early or catch-up MMR doses for people as young as 6 months who aren't fully protected.

"These deaths are entirely preventable," said Dr. Paul Offit, director of the Vaccine Education Center and an infectious disease physician at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia.

Last year, the US reported its first measles deaths in decades, including two unvaccinated children in Texas.

articles.body: National Medical Commission (NMC) is seeking to re-register around 11 lakh doctors to create an updated national medical registry, yet it has failed to register even fresh entrants to the profession despite many state registries sharing records every year, reports Rema Nagarajan.Based on MBBS seats and pass rates, at least 68,000 new doctors should have registered to practice, but only 44,400 entries were recorded in 2025 with at least 24,000 graduates missing in Indian Medical Register. The gap points to potential failure of NMC to sync state and national registries, as required under NMC Act.NMC pushes old docs to re-register, but canât net new onesThe National Medical Commission (NMC) is pushing a regulation to make about 11 lakh doctors re-register to create an updated national medical registry, but it has failed to even register fresh entrants to the profession despite many state registries sending it new entries every year.With over 91,000 MBBS seats available in 2020-21, even with an estimated 75-90% pass percentage, at least 68,000 MBBS graduates should have registered to practice in 2025. Yet the Indian Medical Register shows just over 44,400 entries. That means at least 24,000 of those who graduated just last year are missing from the registry.If thousands of foreign medical graduates who register each year are included, the number of freshly minted doctors missing from the registry would be even more. For instance, in 2023, over 10,000 foreign medical graduates passed the qualifying exam, after which they have to complete a mandatory one-year internship before receiving permanent registration that would make them eligible to practice in India. So, most of these 10,000 would have registered in 2025. Thus, the total number of doctors registering in 2025 would be roughly 80,000, but just over half the number (55%) have been added to the registry.Most of the doctors would have registered with state medical councils. However, new entries in state medical council registries are not being reflected in the national registry as the NMC is yet to synchronise all state registries with the national registry. The NMC Act, 2019, had mandated such synchronisation. It is yet to happen, almost six years after the NMC was constituted in Sept 2020. Neither is NMC adding the new entries that many state councils send every year.Take Assam Medical Council, for instance. It is a state with only govt medical colleges. In the national registry, there are a total of 25,722 registrations from the state council. It shows only one entry for 2025, zero for 2024 and 2023, 106 entries for 2022 and 353 in 2021. The website shows 890 registered in 2024. There were over 720 seats in Assam in 2015 and 1,000 seats in 2020. How is NMC accepting zero entries in 2023 and 2024, or only 106 in 2022?Similarly, NMCâs registry has a total of 67,142 entries from Kerala with just seven entries in 2025 and 17 in 2024. In 2014, Kerala had 3,650 MBBS seats, which increased to 4,500 by 2020. âWe are sending details every year... In the name of a new updated NMR, they are not updating the existing one,â said KSMC chief Dr Harikumaran Nair.If the NMC were to register only those who became doctors in the last five years, including foreign medical graduates, it would have had an updated registry of over 3.5 lakh doctors (32%) of the estimated 11 lakh who are said to be available.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: New mom woke to find baby "blue and cold"—She knew exactly what to do
articles.summary: A Missouri mom describes the horrifying moment she found her newborn unresponsive and sprang into action.
articles.body:
A new mom has described the moment she woke up to find her newborn daughter "blue and cold" and what she did next.

Layna Wells, of Missouri, said there was nothing out of the ordinary about that particular morning. She woke up at 5 a.m. to feed her 3-week-old daughter, Stevie, burped her, and held her for about 15 to 20 minutes before laying her back down to sleep.

Wells said it was around 7 a.m. when she next woke to every new parent's worst nightmare.

"I don't know why I woke up, but I did," she told Newsweek . "I rolled over to see my daughter blue and cold."

Unswaddling Stevie's limp, blue body, Wells immediately sprang into action.

"I immediately turned her over, did the five blows between the shoulders, turned her over again and did the compressions," she said.

That was when she noticed Stevie had started to breathe again.

"I started to aggressively massage her skin to make sure the blood was flowing properly, and that's when her eyes opened," Wells said. "She didn't cry."

Wells said Stevie was awake all the way to the ER but "never cried" during the journey.

"When they started checking her vitals and took her temperature, that's when she started to cry for the first time since CPR, and that was well over an hour later," Wells said.

She was diagnosed with a Brief Resolved Unexplained Event (BRUE).

A BRUE is a brief, unexplained episode in an infant that has resolved by the time medical care is sought. While the event can be frightening for parents, modern pediatric guidance views BRUE as distinct from Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS) and Sudden Unexpected Infant Death (SUID), and most infants who experience a low-risk BRUE have excellent outcomes and are not at increased risk of sudden infant death.

Historically, a predecessor term called ALTE (Apparent Life-Threatening Event) was studied partly because doctors wondered whether it might be linked to SIDS. However, research over time found that most of these events were not precursors to SIDS , which led the American Academy of Pediatrics to replace ALTE with the more specific term BRUE in 2016.

"There was no reason for why it happened," Wells said. "Nothing clogged her airways. Her heart was healthy. Her oxygen levels were fine. Overall, she seemed healthy on all of her scans."

Though Wells administered CPR to Stevie at the time, she later realized she had done so "incorrectly." Nevertheless, it had the desired effect, with Wells saying doctors told her that "if it ever happens again, do exactly what you did."

The incident has haunted Wells ever since.

"It's by far the most gut-wrenching, horrible, nauseating experience I've ever lived through," she said. "I had a glimpse of what it would feel like to lose her, and I now have 10 seconds of a pain I'll forever be terrified to feel again."

There are still nights when she struggles to sleep with Stevie nearby.

"I just sit there and watch her breathe," she said. "Sometimes her breathing slows down and I go into immediate panic mode."

Wells hopes her story inspires other parents to learn infant CPR.

"You never think you're actually going to need to use it until suddenly you do, and in that moment you don't have time to Google what to do or second-guess yourself," she said.

However, she also believes she got "incredibly lucky" that morning.

"I happened to find my daughter when I did, I was able to react, and thankfully what I did worked," she said.

"I never want another parent to hear my story and think that if they had just checked one more time, known CPR better, or done something differently, their outcome would have been different. Sometimes parents do everything right and still experience an unimaginable loss. That is not a failure on their part."

articles.title: Was Bronny James actually traded to the Sixers? What really happened
articles.summary: Some headlines suggested that Bronny James was traded.
articles.body:
When LeBron James opted to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers for the final stage of his legendary NBA career, there were obvious questions about what that meant for his son, Bronny James .

And there are some sites that are taking advantage of those questions.

Bronny was drafted by the Lakers in the second round in 2024 despite playing sparingly in one season at USC amid suffering cardiac arrest. The learning curve was always going to be steep for Bronny in the NBA, and LeBron's presence on the Lakers was the driving force behind Bronny ending up in Los Angeles .

But Bronny is still under contract with the Lakers and has not been traded .

Why are headlines claiming Bronny has been traded?

The website, TotalProSports, created a "trade proposal" blog but crafted a headline as if it was reporting a real trade. But the trade in question was total fiction.

By claiming that Bronny landed with the Sixers in a "blockbuster three-team trade," TotalProSports was able to fool search algorithms and use syndication agreements (such as with Yahoo! Sports ) to its advantage and get prominent placement.

It's a shady headline practice that is closer to lying than it is to creating content in good faith.

Aug 25 (Reuters) - The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Tuesday reported 17,180 confirmed ‌cases of cyclosporiasis in the United States, ‌an increase of 1,464 cases from a week ago.

• The CDC said it has received reports of 17,180 confirmed cases across 48 states plus the District of Columbia, with 922 hospitalizations and two deaths ‌as of August 24. ⁠At least 11,844 additional cases may require further investigation and analysis, CDC said.

• ⁠The data include the cases reported in the ongoing multistate outbreak linked to recalled iceberg lettuce, CDC ​said, adding ​that it is investigating ​multiple clusters of cyclosporiasis.

• ‌CDC and FDA are investigating at least six other clusters for which sources have not yet been confirmed, CDC said.

• Michigan, the hardest-hit state, logged a slow 3% rise to 14,277 last week, hinting ‌the outbreak may be easing.

• ​The cyclosporiasis outbreak is one ​of the largest foodborne ​illness events in recent U.S. history. ‌The illness is caused by ​the cyclospora ​parasite, which can lead to diarrhea, nausea and other gastrointestinal symptoms.

• The outbreak has shaken U.S. ​consumers nationwide, causing ‌many to forgo eating fresh produce or ​dining in restaurants.

(Reporting by Christy Santhosh in Bengaluru; ​Editing by Vijay Kishore)

articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The cost of the Ahmedabad-Mumbai bullet train has been revised to around Rs 2.1 lakh crore, nearly double the original cost of approximatel.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The cost of the Ahmedabad-Mumbai bullet train has been revised to around Rs 2.1 lakh crore, nearly double the original cost of approximately Rs 1.1 lakh crore. The proposal to seek approval for the revised cost of the 508-km high-speed rail line was placed before the Cabinet Tuesday, TOI has learnt.Sources said the railway ministry has cited the time taken in land acquisition in Maharashtra and delay in getting the train sets from Japan as among the main reasons for the cost escalation. They added the project is likely to be completed in 2030 and the first leg of the corridor is scheduled to be operational in Aug 2027.Sources said most of the additional funding would come from budgetary support. So far, the funding of Rs 1.1 lakh crore has been from Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) and budgetary allocation. They added that Railways has said high-speed trains will be manufactured in India and each of these would cost around Rs 390 crore to Rs 400 crore. There was no official briefing on the decisions of the Cabinet meeting chaired by PM Narendra Modi.In Jan, railway board chairperson Satish Kumar had said the project cost had increased by around 83% to Rs 1.98 lakh crore. The project has faced time and cost overruns due to many reasons, including delay in land acquisition, statutory clearances and finalisation of the trains.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: How to buy travel insurance (and when to skip it)
articles.summary: Learn how to buy travel insurance, compare coverage, and choose the right policy for your next trip without overpaying.
articles.body:

Planning a vacation is exciting, but buying travel insurance can feel like homework. Between comparing plans, checking what your credit card already covers, and sorting through policy fine print, it's easy to get bogged down in the details before you even pack your bags.

Here's everything you need to know about how to buy travel insurance without the guesswork.

You don't need travel insurance for every trip. If you're driving two hours to visit family, a standalone policy is probably overkill. But if you're spending thousands of dollars up front — or leaving the country — travel insurance deserves a second look.

Travel insurance is most useful for protecting prepaid, nonrefundable costs and covering medical emergencies. Purchasing a policy makes the most sense if you're taking an international trip, cruise, safari, luxury tour, or any vacation where you'd lose a meaningful amount of money if you had to cancel.

It's also worth considering if you're traveling during hurricane season, visiting a remote destination, traveling with small children or older relatives, or have health issues that could complicate your itinerary.

In other words, the more expensive, complex, or medically risky the trip, the more it makes sense to purchase coverage.

Before you buy a standalone travel insurance policy, it pays to check what protection you already have. Your health insurance, credit card, or homeowners insurance might offer benefits that could save you money.

Health insurance plans usually include some protection when you travel, especially for emergency care within the U.S. Many plans cover out-of-network emergency services, and some employer-sponsored plans offer limited international benefits or overseas claims support.

For example, Blue Cross and Blue Shield's Federal Employee Program says members can submit claims for medical services received overseas and use an international provider finder.

But details vary. A plan that works well across state lines might offer little or no coverage abroad, and even robust medical plans won't pay for trip cancellations or baggage delays.

Older travelers in particular should check their health coverage before departure. Original Medicare includes very limited coverage outside the U.S., though some Medigap policies cover foreign travel emergency care. Medicare Advantage plans may include travel perks, but they can also enforce network rules that make routine care away from home more complicated.

The best way to find out what your plan actually covers is to call your insurer directly or check your plan documents.

Many travel credit cards include some travel protections. Credit card benefits can include trip cancellation, trip interruption, trip delay, baggage delay, lost luggage reimbursement, and rental car damage coverage.

While it's less common, some premium credit cards, such as Chase Sapphire Reserve, offer cardmembers limited emergency medical and evacuation benefits. However, even premium credit cards might exclude preexisting conditions.

Using your card's benefits usually requires documentation from the travel provider. So report the issue to the airline, hotel, or cruise line first and get written confirmation. Also, check your card's deadline for notifying the benefits administrator, a third-party insurer listed in the card's guide to benefits.

You'll typically need to prove you paid for the trip with that credit card, document what went wrong, and show what costs remain. In many cases, credit card coverage is secondary, meaning it will reimburse expenses only after the airline, travel provider, or another insurance policy pays first.

The best move is to review your card's guide to benefits before you buy a policy. If the card already covers trip and baggage delays, you might only need to shop for a standalone travel medical policy to fill in that gap. The good news is that medical-only travel insurance plans tend to be much cheaper than comprehensive travel policies.

Your homeowners or renters insurance may help if your belongings are stolen or damaged while you're traveling. That's because these policies can include personal property coverage that follows your belongings even when you're away from home. So if your laptop is stolen during a trip, you can file a claim for the item.

However, homeowners and renters insurance usually won't help with trip cancellation, medical bills, missed connections, or travel delays.

There are also limits. Your deductible may be higher than the value of the lost item. Expensive jewelry, cameras, electronics, or collectibles may have sublimits.

Travel insurance typically bundles several different benefits into a single policy, but each plan is different. Some policies are comprehensive, while others only cover medical emergencies.

Common travel insurance benefits include:

Trip cancellation coverage: Reimburses prepaid, nonrefundable costs if you cancel before departure for a covered reason, such as illness, injury, severe weather, or the death of a family member.

Trip interruption coverage: Helps pay if you need to cut a trip short and return home for a covered reason. It can reimburse unused trip costs and extra transportation.

Travel delay coverage: Reimburses reasonable expenses, such as meals, lodging, and toiletries, if your trip is delayed long enough to meet the policy's waiting period.

Missed connection coverage: Can help pay transportation costs if a covered delay makes you miss a cruise or tour departure.

Emergency medical coverage: Pays for covered medical treatment if you get sick or injured during your trip.

Emergency medical evacuation: Helps cover transportation to an appropriate medical facility or, in serious cases, back home.

Baggage loss or damage: Reimburses you if your luggage or belongings are lost, stolen, or damaged, up to the policy's limits.

Baggage delay : Pays for essentials if your checked bag is delayed beyond the policy's waiting period.

Travel assistance services: Usually a toll-free 1-800 number or app offered by the insurer that can help with referrals, translation, lost passports, emergency cash transfers, and coordination during medical emergencies.

This is where travelers can get burned. Standard travel insurance covers specific situations listed in the policy, but it isn't a blank check for everything that can possibly go wrong on your trip.

Trip cancellation coverage is especially strict, which is why some travelers opt for cancel-for-any-reason (CFAR) coverage. It's a premium add-on that increases your policy's cost, but it might be worth considering if you want the flexibility.

Common travel insurance exclusions include:

Foreseeable events, such as a hurricane that was already named before you bought the policy

Changing your mind, unless you bought cancel-for-any-reason coverage

Preexisting medical conditions, unless your plan includes a waiver and you meet the requirements

Routine medical care, checkups, or elective procedures

Losses involving intoxication, illegal acts, or reckless behavior

High-risk or adventure activities, such as skydiving, backcountry skiing, or scuba diving

Other scenarios may or may not be covered, depending on your policy, such as war, civil unrest, pandemics, or your cruise line (or other travel supplier) going bankrupt.

Always read the exclusions section carefully before buying. It's boring, but it can help avoid unpleasant surprises if you need to file a claim later.

A comprehensive travel insurance policy often costs about 4% to 10% of your total prepaid, nonrefundable trip cost, according to InsureMyTrip, a travel insurance comparison site. That means a $5,000 trip might cost roughly $250 to $500 to insure.

However, your actual cost depends on your age, trip cost, trip length, destination, and coverage amounts. Older travelers pay more because their medical risk is higher. Longer trips and more expensive trips also cost more to insure.

Medical-only policies are more affordable on average than comprehensive plans because they don't cover the full cost of your trip. That can make sense if your flights and hotels are refundable, but your health insurance plan doesn't offer coverage abroad.

Cancel-for-any-reason coverage costs extra. It can raise your premium significantly — about $55 a day extra, according to Squaremouth, a travel insurance comparison site — and usually reimburses only 50% to 75% of your costs.

Timing matters more than many travelers realize. You can't simply buy travel insurance right before you leave for the airport.

In some cases, waiting too long can limit the benefits you're eligible for, so the earlier you buy coverage, the more options you'll have.

That's especially true if you want a preexisting medical condition waiver or CFAR coverage. These benefits are usually available only if you buy the policy within a set time frame after your first trip payment, usually 14 to 21 days. You may also need to insure the full prepaid, nonrefundable cost of the trip and be medically able to travel when you buy the policy.

CFAR coverage also usually requires you to cancel at least 48 to 72 hours before departure, though the exact rules vary by insurer.

If you missed that 14- to 21-day window, don't worry — you can still likely secure a basic policy.

However, you can't buy insurance after something happens (such as a job loss or death of a family member) and expect coverage to apply for that event. Once the hurricane is named, your doctor tells you not to travel, or your airline announces a strike, it's probably too late to buy coverage.

How to buy travel insurance: Step by step

When shopping for travel insurance, the goal isn't to buy the most expensive policy or the cheapest one. The goal is to protect yourself from the risks you couldn't easily pay for out of pocket.

Start by adding up all your prepaid, nonrefundable trip costs, including flights, hotels, and other bookings you'd lose money on if you had to cancel.

Don't include refundable costs. If you can cancel a hotel for free or get an airline credit you'd actually use, you may not need to insure that full amount.

Once you have the total, ask whether you could comfortably eat that loss. If the answer is yes, you might not need much trip cancellation coverage. If the answer is no, a comprehensive policy might make sense.

Step 2: Decide which benefits you really need

You don't need to be an expert on every available travel insurance benefit. Instead, look at your itinerary and ask what would be expensive or difficult to fix if something went wrong.

If you're leaving the U.S., look closely at emergency medical and medical evacuation coverage . Your regular health insurance may not travel well overseas, and an emergency evacuation can cost $100,000 or more, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

If you have any sort of chronic or on-going medical condition — from asthma to arthritis — securing a preexisting condition waiver is key. Without it, the insurer can deny your claim if the medical issue on your trip is tied to that condition.

If you're taking a cruise or guided tour, missed-connection and trip-interruption coverage become more important. A delayed flight isn't merely an inconvenience if it causes you to miss the ship or the start of a prepaid tour.

Once you've identified the coverage that matters most, it's easier to shop around and compare policies.

Step 3: Check what coverage you already have

Before gathering quotes, review the protections you might already have through your health insurance, credit card, homeowners insurance, or renters insurance.

This step requires some additional research, but it's worth it. There's no point in buying duplicate coverage if you can avoid it.

Next, get quotes from a travel insurance comparison marketplace, such as Squaremouth or InsureMyTrip. You can also buy directly from an insurer or through a travel agent, but comparison sites are the best way to explore all your options side by side.

To get started, enter your destination, travel dates, age, state of residence, and total trip cost. You can also filter your results based on price or the benefits you're most interested in, such as a preexisting condition waiver.

Once you've narrowed down your options to a few plans, read the policy certificate for each one. This is the document where you'll find the fine print on what's covered, what's excluded, and how much the insurer will pay.

Watch for restrictions around preexisting conditions, adventure activities, and foreseeable events. A cheaper policy might work well, but only if it covers the situations you're actually worried about.

Step 5: Buy the policy and save your documents

Once you've identified a plan that fits your budget and needs, it's time to buy. Make sure the traveler names, trip dates, destination, and insured trip cost are correct.

Finally, make sure to save the policy certificate, claim instructions, and emergency assistance number in a couple safe locations. Keep receipts and booking confirmations, too. If you need to file a claim, the insurer will need documentation.

How far in advance should I buy travel insurance?

Most experts recommend buying a policy as soon as you make your first trip payment. This way, you'll get access to time-sensitive benefits, such as preexisting condition waivers and CFAR coverage.

Does travel insurance cover trip cancellation for any reason?

Standard travel insurance doesn't. It only covers cancellations for reasons listed in the policy. To cancel for almost any reason, you generally need to buy CFAR coverage as an optional upgrade.

Is travel insurance worth it for domestic trips?

Sometimes. It might be worth it if the trip is expensive and mostly nonrefundable. However, travel insurance usually doesn't make sense for a cheap domestic trip with refundable bookings and decent health insurance coverage.

Can I buy travel insurance after booking my trip?

Yes. You can usually buy travel insurance after booking, and sometimes up until shortly before departure. However, some benefits are available only if you buy within a limited window after your first trip payment.

When to buy travel insurance (and when it's too late)

Waiting too long to buy travel insurance can limit your options. Here's when to buy coverage — and when it might be too late.
